title: Sharpness-Aware Minimization: General Analysis and Improved Rates
main_claims: A Unified SAM update rule is proposed as a convex combination of SAM and USAM (parameterized by λ∈[0,1]), unifying both variants and enabling analysis of novel sampling strategies.
Convergence guarantees for Unified SAM are established under the Expected Residual (ER) condition, which is weaker than the bounded variance assumption used in all prior SAM analyses.

In the deterministic full-batch setting, USAM (λ=0) converges exactly to the solution for PL functions while SAM (λ=1) converges only to a neighborhood, confirming a previously observed empirical gap.
methodology: Stochastic reformulation of the finite-sum optimization problem using arbitrary sampling vectors allows uniform treatment of SAM and USAM. The ER condition replaces bounded variance/gradient assumptions. Main theorems cover: (i) linear convergence for PL functions with constant step sizes, (ii) exact convergence with O(1/t) rate for PL functions with decreasing step sizes, (iii) general non-convex convergence at sublinear rate. Importance sampling probabilities proportional to individual smoothness constants are derived. Numerical experiments validate theoretical predictions and demonstrate Unified SAM on CIFAR image classification.
key_results: Unified SAM with constant step sizes achieves linear convergence to a neighborhood for µ-PL functions without bounded variance assumption.
Decreasing step sizes achieve exact O(1/t) convergence for PL functions — the first such result for SAM.
In the deterministic setting, USAM converges exactly to the minimizer while SAM converges only to a neighborhood (gap = Lmax·ρ(1+2γL²max·ρ)λ²/µ).
Importance sampling with probabilities proportional to individual Li constants provably improves the iteration complexity bound.
limitations: Results are primarily theoretical; the practical impact of the improved convergence rates over vanilla SAM for real deep learning tasks is not fully quantified.
The Unified SAM framework does not cover all SAM variants (e.g. ASAM, GSAM) explicitly.
ER condition, while weaker than bounded variance, still requires some regularity; it may not hold for all practical distributions.
relevance_to_rq: Peripheral to the core RQ: provides theoretical convergence analysis of SAM but does not address OOD generalization, CIFAR-C, or the comparison with SWA. Relevant background for understanding SAM's optimization properties, which inform why SAM and SWA may differ in their solutions.
